topic: Toji's zero cursed energy is the one thing Gojo's defenses were never built to answer, so he alone had a real path to ending Gojo
title: Toji Was The Only Sorcerer Who Could Have Ended Gojo
description:
Toji Fushiguro had a real path to ending Satoru Gojo, and no other sorcerer in Jujutsu Kaisen ever did. This breakdown walks the Hidden Inventory fight, Toji's zero cursed energy, and why Infinity and the Six Eyes had nothing to grab.

We cover chapters 67 to 75, Toji's reflexes in the Dagon fight, Maki's Heavenly Restriction, and the best counter-argument: Sukuna in chapter 236. Who do you think came closest, Toji or Sukuna?
comment: Who came closer to ending Gojo: Toji with zero cursed energy, or Sukuna with the space-cutting trick? Pick one.

lines.text: Toji Fushiguro is the only sorcerer in Jujutsu Kaisen who ever had a real path to ending Satoru Gojo.

shot.search: Toji Fushiguro Gojo fight Hidden Inventory
shot.fallback: dark haired scarred fighter facing a white haired sorcerer in a hallway

lines.text: Gojo has Infinity, the Six Eyes and Hollow Purple. So how does a man with no cursed energy get through any of it?

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer with glowing blue eyes behind a shimmering barrier

lines.text: Because every defense Gojo owns is built to read cursed energy, and Toji is the one man who gives it nothing to read...

shot.fallback: silhouette of a muscular man with no aura standing in the dark

lines.text: Chapter 71 is where it nearly worked. Then come three reasons nobody else gets that opening, and one objection I can't fully beat...

shot.fallback: two fighters circling in a courtyard at dusk

lines.text: Start with what the jujutsu world got wrong. Toji was born with no cursed energy at all, and the Zenin clan wrote him off.

shot.fallback: young man in a dark haori walking past stern elders

lines.text: That is a Heavenly Restriction, and Yuki Tsukumo found that his is the only case where cursed energy was erased completely.

shot.fallback: blonde woman in a long coat explaining to a young man

lines.text: In exchange, his senses sharpened so far that he could see curses with plain eyes and track sorcerers by footprints and smell. That's chapter 73.

shot.fallback: man crouching and studying footprints on a dirt road

lines.text: Here's the part most people skip. With no cursed energy, sorcerers can't detect him, and that includes the Six Eyes.

shot.search: Toji Gojo Six Eyes invisible man
shot.fallback: blue glowing eyes searching an empty room

lines.text: Barriers treat him like scenery, so he walks into places built to keep sorcerers out. Chapter 110.

shot.search: Toji Fushiguro barrier Tombs of the Star
shot.fallback: man stepping calmly through a glowing barrier

lines.text: Think about what Gojo's whole toolkit runs on. Every technique he owns uses cursed energy, and every defense reads it.

shot.fallback: blue and red spheres of energy glowing in a sorcerer's hands

lines.text: Infinity, the Six Eyes watching the flow, Blue pulling and Red pushing. Take the energy away and those tools have nothing to grab.

shot.search: Gojo Infinity Lapse Blue Reversal Red
shot.fallback: swirling blue vortex pulling debris inward

lines.text: Thanks to the Six Eyes, Gojo burns almost no cursed energy, so he never seems to run dry. Chapters 140 and 225 show it.

shot.search: Gojo Six Eyes cursed energy efficiency
shot.fallback: calm white haired sorcerer with a faint blue glow

lines.text: But efficiency means nothing against an opponent who was never part of that system in the first place.

shot.fallback: two fighters staring each other down

lines.text: So the Zenin verdict on Toji is the biggest misread in the setting. They measured the wrong number.

shot.fallback: elders looking down at a lone man in a hall

lines.text: Toji also wasn't just invisible. Megumi calls him faster than Sukuna with three fingers in chapter 111.

shot.fallback: dark haired teen staring in shock at a blurred fast figure

lines.text: He even stepped out of Gojo's Blue before Gojo understood what he was looking at. Chapter 71.

shot.fallback: man sidestepping a collapsing swirl of blue energy

lines.text: Add a cursed tool sword, knives and the Inverted Spear of Heaven, and he's built to answer sorcerers one at a time.

shot.fallback: man holding a jagged ornate spear

lines.text: The Zenin clan also knew how Limitless works, and Toji carried that knowledge out the door. Chapter 75.

shot.fallback: man reading scrolls in a dim clan library

lines.text: So he had the body, the tools and the manual. But a body alone never opens that lock...

shot.fallback: stoic scarred man in a black shirt

lines.text: Because Toji didn't get near it with power. He got there with patience, and it started with a stranger's greed...

shot.fallback: shadowy figure at a desk with money and a laptop

lines.text: Chapter 67 gives us the first piece, and it's colder than you'd expect from a man who never drew attention.

shot.search: Toji Fushiguro bounty Star Plasma Vessel
shot.fallback: man gambling at a card table at night

lines.text: Toji put a bounty on Riko Amanai, the Star Plasma Vessel, on a site for curse users, with a time limit attached.

shot.fallback: glowing computer screen with a countdown timer

lines.text: Evil sorcerers rushed to collect, and Toji knew they would lose, so he got free labor wearing down the escort.

shot.search: Gojo Geto escort Riko Amanai attackers
shot.fallback: two students escorting a girl through a crowded city

lines.text: Here's what I think nobody noticed about that timer. It didn't just draw fighters, it taught Gojo when to stop paying attention.

shot.search: Gojo Riko Amanai Tokyo Jujutsu High
shot.fallback: white haired student relaxing as he waits

lines.text: Look at who he was up against. Satoru Gojo and Suguru Geto were the strongest students in the school.

shot.fallback: two young sorcerers in dark uniforms standing together

lines.text: The Star Religious Group funded him, and the mission Tengen gave them was guarding Riko across several days.

shot.search: Star Religious Group Riko Amanai Tengen
shot.fallback: girl in a school uniform walking beside two sorcerers

lines.text: Over those days, small tactical moves from Toji kept derailing the escort until the team felt safe. Chapter 74.

shot.fallback: tired students on a quiet street at night

lines.text: The mission ended on a high. Riko reached the Tombs of the Star, and Gojo finally switched Infinity off...

shot.search: Gojo deactivates Infinity Tombs of the Star
shot.fallback: relaxed sorcerer lowering his guard in a shrine courtyard

lines.text: That's the moment Toji was waiting for. He didn't win a contest of power, he waited for the lock to open.

shot.search: Toji Fushiguro appears Gojo Infinity off
shot.fallback: dark figure stepping out of shadow behind a relaxed sorcerer

lines.text: I think that's the real story of Hidden Inventory. It isn't a duel, it's a trap with a patient hunter and a relaxed guard.

shot.fallback: shadowy man behind a relaxed sorcerer

lines.text: That's chapter 71, and it is the single most important fact in this breakdown. Everything else is a footnote to it.

shot.fallback: shocked student at the moment an attack lands

lines.text: Infinity is not a switch that stays on forever. It takes attention, and even the Six Eyes cannot hold it open every second of a mission.

shot.fallback: glowing barrier flickering around a sorcerer

lines.text: Toji used exactly that gap, and he came through it with a blade into Gojo's chest.

shot.search: Toji Gojo blade chest Hidden Inventory
shot.fallback: two fighters meeting with a flash of impact

lines.text: Gojo reinforced his body with cursed energy, so the blade did far less than it should have. That detail is easy to miss.

shot.search: Gojo cursed energy reinforcement Toji sword
shot.fallback: student gritting his teeth as a blue glow covers him

lines.text: Even so, Toji left both of the school's most gifted students nearly finished in one afternoon, with only a small cut at his own ear.

shot.fallback: two battered students against a wall while a man walks away

lines.text: Geto's attempt shows how thin the margin was. He tried to cut off Toji's weapon supply by absorbing the inventory curse.

shot.fallback: dark haired student summoning a huge cursed spirit

lines.text: That nearly worked, and then it backfired in a way Geto couldn't have seen coming. Chapter 73.

shot.fallback: student recoiling from a ripped open cursed spirit

lines.text: Toji called Geto's abilities rabble next to his own strength, and the fight records back him up. That's chapter 73.

shot.fallback: scarred man dismissing a dark haired student

lines.text: Toji later said blessed talents lost to a man who can't use jujutsu. Chapter 73. But was that skill, or luck?

shot.search: Toji tells Geto Gojo lost monkey
shot.fallback: scarred man looking down at two students on the ground

lines.text: To answer that, look at the Dagon fight, when Toji came back through Ogami's Séance Technique in the Shibuya Incident.

shot.fallback: old woman performing a ritual with a possessed grandson

lines.text: Dagon, a special grade curse, had beaten Maki, Nanami and Naobito Zenin together. Toji made exorcising it look easy.

shot.search: Toji Dagon fight Shibuya Playful Cloud
shot.fallback: man swinging a huge staff at a giant sea creature

lines.text: He took Playful Cloud from Maki's hands as if it weighed nothing, then used it at full strength. Chapter 110.

shot.search: Toji takes Playful Cloud from Maki
shot.fallback: man pulling a giant weapon out of a woman's grip

lines.text: Megumi saw the same thing from the other side. He called Toji a monster who could take out a special grade. Chapter 113.

shot.fallback: dark haired teen staring at a towering figure

lines.text: That's not luck. That's a man who needs no cursed energy to beat a special grade.

shot.fallback: calm man standing over a defeated sea curse

lines.text: So his edge is repeatable. But what stopped him at the end of the Hidden Inventory fight?

shot.fallback: two fighters facing each other in a courtyard

lines.text: Gojo himself, in the very moment he looked beaten. And that is where the story turns...

shot.search: Gojo awakens Reverse Cursed Technique Toji
shot.fallback: white haired student rising with a faint blue glow

lines.text: What happened next is the other half of my argument, because it shows why a second chance never came.

shot.fallback: determined sorcerer facing an armed man

lines.text: After the first exchange, Gojo had Toji's measure and Toji had a plan for Limitless. Both of them kept fighting.

shot.fallback: fighters trading blows while energy bends around them

lines.text: Toji attached a chain to the Inverted Spear of Heaven and switched to a long-range style. That's chapter 75.

shot.search: Toji chain Inverted Spear of Heaven
shot.fallback: man swinging a chained spear in a wide arc

lines.text: The Zenin clan's knowledge of Limitless guided that choice, and Gojo had to improvise on the spot.

shot.fallback: man studying his opponent's technique with narrowed eyes

lines.text: Here's what that rush taught Gojo: a cursed energy defense can be bypassed without being broken.

shot.search: Gojo learns Reverse Cursed Technique Toji
shot.fallback: wide eyed student realizing something

lines.text: He used that life-and-death moment to understand reverse cursed technique, and it changed what he could do.

shot.fallback: glowing white energy surrounding a sorcerer's hands

lines.text: That one realization is why Toji's window closed. The same attack could never land the same way twice.

shot.fallback: huge purple orb of energy forming between two hands

lines.text: Only Hollow Purple was strong enough to put Toji down for good. That's chapter 75, and it ended the fight.

shot.fallback: massive purple beam tearing across a landscape

lines.text: Even then, Toji used his final moments for something else. He pictured Megumi and told Gojo to do what he liked with the boy.

shot.fallback: tired man thinking of a small child

lines.text: Toji told him that Megumi would be sold to the Zenin clan in a few years, so Gojo would know where to look.

shot.search: Toji sells Megumi Zenin clan Gojo
shot.fallback: small boy standing in a traditional house

lines.text: That one sentence is how Gojo became Megumi's guardian, according to chapter 59. It changed the whole future of the story.

shot.fallback: tall man standing beside a quiet boy

lines.text: Toji's pride matters here. The wiki notes he should have cut and run, but spite for the jujutsu world kept him in the fight. Chapter 75.

shot.fallback: stubborn man refusing to step back

lines.text: He ignored the uneasiness gnawing at him during the fight, and I think that single lapse is why the opening closed. Chapter 75.

shot.fallback: man frowning mid battle

lines.text: So the first fight ended with Gojo alive, stronger, and holding a debt to the man who nearly ended him. Why couldn't anyone else do it?

shot.fallback: sorcerer carrying a girl through the rain

lines.text: The answer comes in three parts, and each one rules out a famous name that fans always bring up.

shot.fallback: confident white haired sorcerer smiling at his enemies

lines.text: Reason one is the cursed energy itself. Every other fighter in the series has some, and Gojo's senses can pick it up.

shot.search: Gojo Six Eyes cursed energy flow
shot.fallback: glowing blue eyes watching a stream of energy

lines.text: Take Geto, a powerful grade 1 who rose to special grade. His strategy depends on cursed spirits that Gojo can see coming.

shot.fallback: dark haired sorcerer commanding a giant cursed spirit

lines.text: Same for Jogo and Hanami. They tried domain amplification against Infinity, and Gojo pushed it outward and crushed Hanami against a wall. Chapter 85.

shot.search: Gojo Jogo Hanami Infinity domain amplification
shot.fallback: volcano headed curse in front of a plant spirit

lines.text: Both came at Gojo through cursed energy, so both ran into the very thing Gojo's Limitless was designed to manage.

shot.fallback: volcano headed curse launching fire at a sorcerer

lines.text: Reason two is domains. A domain expansion hits with a sure-hit attack, and that attack relies on the target's cursed energy.

shot.search: Domain Expansion sure-hit Gojo Unlimited Void
shot.fallback: sorcerer clasping hands inside a galaxy-like space

lines.text: Maki has no cursed energy at all, and her chapter says domains can't target her. She's the modern proof of the rule.

shot.search: Maki Zenin no cursed energy domain
shot.fallback: woman with short hair walking calmly through a barrier

lines.text: So the counter to Gojo's strongest tools follows Toji's logic, but Maki wasn't there yet when it mattered.

shot.search: Maki Zenin Heavenly Restriction Toji comparison
shot.fallback: woman with a sword standing among defeated clan members

lines.text: Chapter 151 shows her body reaching Toji's level, and chapter 152 shows she can't be tracked once her cursed energy is gone.

shot.fallback: woman in a ruined clan estate under a pale moon

lines.text: But in chapter 190, Maki is still told she lacks what made Toji, Toji. She was never his equal until her mindset changed.

shot.fallback: woman training alone beside a quiet river

lines.text: Naoya refused to accept Maki as Toji's successor in strength, and she beat him anyway. That's chapter 151.

shot.fallback: woman standing over a defeated arrogant man

lines.text: A lot of fans forget this. Zero cursed energy isn't enough, you need Toji's mindset too.

shot.fallback: woman breaking free from chains in a dark room

lines.text: Reason three is planning. Toji spent days preparing a single opening, and he was ready to leave if it didn't come.

shot.fallback: man studying a map and a clock at a table

lines.text: Nobody else who fought Gojo treated patience as a weapon. They came in wanting a fight, and Gojo has always loved a fight.

shot.fallback: grinning white haired sorcerer cracking his knuckles

lines.text: Toji was the only one who treated Gojo like a mission instead of a rival. That's the difference.

shot.fallback: calm assassin watching a target from a rooftop

lines.text: Put those three reasons together: no cursed energy, a body built for sorcerers, and a plan built around one slip.

shot.search: Toji Fushiguro Gojo Satoru face off
shot.fallback: two powerful fighters framed in a doorway

lines.text: Add Toji's cursed tools. The Inverted Spear of Heaven is his trump card against techniques like Limitless, and it's a special grade tool.

shot.search: Inverted Spear of Heaven special grade cursed tool
shot.fallback: glowing jagged spear on a dark background

lines.text: A caveat here. The search results I found only support that the spear counters techniques on contact, so I'll treat the finer rules as my read.

shot.search: Inverted Spear of Heaven nullifies cursed technique
shot.fallback: spear cutting through a swirl of glowing energy

lines.text: That's an honest limit of this video. I think the spear is more a statement about Toji's fighting style than a cure for Infinity.

shot.search: Toji Inverted Spear of Heaven Gojo
shot.fallback: man gripping a spear in a dim hall

lines.text: Still, the pattern holds. Each time Toji faced a famous sorcerer, he used something that wasn't cursed energy at all.

shot.fallback: table full of knives and swords

lines.text: So the lock has no keyhole for him, he picked his moment, and he still lost in the end. Is that enough to settle it?

shot.fallback: man falling back in front of a purple glow

lines.text: Which brings me to the toughest question. I promised to steelman the best argument against this video...

shot.fallback: two titanic fighters facing each other beneath glowing domains

lines.text: The counter is simple. Sukuna beat Gojo in chapter 236, so doesn't Sukuna deserve the title instead?

shot.fallback: four armed demon king standing triumphant

lines.text: It's a good argument. Sukuna got a technique past Infinity that no sorcerer in the story had managed.

shot.fallback: huge white humanoid with a glowing wheel overhead

lines.text: His trick, as I read chapter 236, was to aim Mahoraga's adapted attack at the space around Gojo instead of Gojo himself.

shot.fallback: white demon aiming a massive blade at empty air

lines.text: Infinity doesn't protect the space around Gojo from being cut, so cutting that space cut him too.

shot.fallback: glowing barrier splitting along a sharp line

lines.text: That's brilliant, and it also needed a lot to go right. A king of curses, an adapted Mahoraga, and a very long fight.

shot.fallback: two exhausted fighters in a ruined city

lines.text: More importantly, Sukuna isn't a sorcerer. He's a Curse King with enormous power behind him, and that changes the comparison.

shot.fallback: four armed demon king on a throne of bones

lines.text: That's the difference in kind. Toji needed no power at all. Sukuna needed a huge amount of it and a lot of help.

shot.fallback: two very different fighters side by side

lines.text: And even then the argument has a limit. Nobody else at Gojo's level ever tried the quiet, planned approach Toji took.

shot.fallback: man waiting patiently in the dark

lines.text: Fans also point to Gojo's fight with Sukuna as proof Gojo wasn't truly invincible. I agree, but it's a different claim.

shot.search: Gojo Unlimited Void Sukuna Malevolent Shrine
shot.fallback: two giant domains clashing over a ruined skyline

lines.text: My claim is narrower. Among sorcerers, meaning humans who fought on that side of the line, Toji was the only one built for it.

shot.fallback: man in black standing over a collapsed rival

lines.text: Here's the other counter, and I can't dismiss it. Gojo was a student, with Infinity switched off, when Toji got through.

shot.search: Gojo Hidden Inventory student Infinity off
shot.fallback: young white haired student in school uniform at ease

lines.text: Adult Gojo never leaves that gap open. Would Toji have found another one, or did Gojo learn the lesson permanently?

shot.search: Gojo adult teacher Tokyo Jujutsu High
shot.fallback: tall blindfolded teacher smiling at his students

lines.text: I think Gojo did learn it. Chapter 75's awakening made him sharper, and he never left that gap open again.

shot.search: Gojo awakening Reverse Cursed Technique Hollow Purple
shot.fallback: sorcerer with glowing hands raised calmly

lines.text: So the strongest version of my claim isn't that Toji would have won. It's that he was the only person who ever had a chance.

shot.fallback: two fighters in a narrow beam of light

lines.text: One more piece ties the two stories together, hidden in how Gojo looks in the final fight...

shot.search: Gojo Shinjuku Showdown outfit no blindfold
shot.fallback: white haired man in dark training clothes without a blindfold

lines.text: Look at what Gojo wears when he faces Sukuna. No blindfold, a tight black shirt, white baggy pants, and slippers.

shot.fallback: white haired fighter in a black shirt and white baggy pants

lines.text: The wiki notes it matches Toji's fighting clothes. That detail is easy to dismiss as a coincidence, but I don't think it is.

shot.fallback: two fighters in matching dark shirts and white pants

lines.text: My read is that Gojo, at his peak, finally respected the style that nearly ended him as a student.

shot.fallback: mirrored silhouettes of two fighters

lines.text: That's a theory, not canon, and I'll label it that way. So where does that leave the verdict?

shot.search: Gojo Sukuna Shinjuku Showdown Toji parallel
shot.fallback: white haired fighter in a combat stance

lines.text: Now zoom back out to the verdict, because the evidence points one way even if the ending didn't.

shot.fallback: three silhouettes lined up on a dark stage

lines.text: Toji had zero cursed energy, so Gojo's defenses had nothing to read, and Gojo's senses couldn't find him.

shot.fallback: man glowing faintly in a dark empty room

lines.text: He was fast enough to dodge Blue, strong enough to take on special grade curses, and patient enough to wait days for one gap.

shot.fallback: man leaning against a wall, waiting

lines.text: He needed Gojo to drop Infinity once, and he nearly turned that one moment into the end of the strongest sorcerer alive.

shot.fallback: man leaping toward a relaxed sorcerer

lines.text: Maki is the only other person who walks the same path, and in the story she never faced Gojo.

shot.fallback: woman holding a sword in a shaft of light

lines.text: Sukuna beat Gojo with a king's power and a clever trick, but he was never a sorcerer, so he isn't part of my claim.

shot.fallback: demon king looking down from a ruin

lines.text: So when people ask who could have ended Gojo, the honest answer is a man the Zenin clan thought was worthless.

shot.fallback: lone man smiling coldly at a clan hall

lines.text: Gojo's greatest strength was reading cursed energy, and his greatest weakness was a man who had none to read.

shot.fallback: blue eyes meeting a blank gaze

lines.text: I still can't decide if Toji's plan was brilliant or if Gojo simply grew up in that exact moment. I lean brilliant.

shot.fallback: man calmly observing a target

lines.text: Toji planned the lock that Gojo left open, and the next story shows how a clan treated its own unwanted sons...

shot.fallback: angry elders in a traditional estate hall

lines.text: If you want to see what happened to the clan that threw him away, the Zenin story is the next one.

shot.fallback: burning traditional estate at night

self_check.hook: Line 1 names Toji and Gojo and claims the path; line 2 asks the core question
self_check.loop: chapters end on open questions; last line points to the Zenin story
